chunks: Sama'ah asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about suhoor for one who intended to fast, so he said:

As for the month of Ramaḍān, the merit is in taking suhoor, even if only with a drink of water. And as for voluntary fasting, whoever likes to take suhoor, let him do so, and whoever does not do so, there is no harm.

key_terms.السَّحُورِ: the pre-dawn meal or drink taken before fasting
key_terms.بِشَرْبَةٍ مِنْ مَاءٍ: even a small drink of water
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the obligatory month of fasting
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection

ai.seo_question: Is suhoor required for fasting in Ramadan and voluntary fasts?
ai.summary: This hadith states that taking suhoor in the month of Ramaḍān is meritorious, even if it consists only of a sip of water. In voluntary fasting, taking suhoor is optional, so one may do it or leave it without blame.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1958 - Sama'ah asked Abu Abdullah (as) about suhoor for someone intending to fast.

Imam (as) said: "As for the Month of Ramadan, it is recommended to have suhoor, even if it is just a sip of water. As for voluntary fasting, whoever wishes to have suhoor may do so, and whoever does not, there is no harm."
